name: Desire (kāma)
description: BhG 4–6: undertakings free of desire mark the learned (4.19); the unyoked is bound, attached to the fruit through the drive of desire (5.12); the surge of desire and anger is to be withstood before leaving the body (5.23); the liberated sage is free of desire (icchā), fear and anger (5.28); the yoked one is free of craving for all desires (6.18); desires born of intention are to be abandoned without remainder (6.24).

name: Anger (krodha)
description: BhG 4–6: those free of passion, fear and anger came to the Lord's being (4.10); the surge of desire and anger is to be withstood (5.23); ascetics free of desire and anger have brahma-nirvāṇa all around them (5.26); the sage from whom desire, fear and anger have gone is ever liberated (5.28).

name: Desire and anger, the enemy (kāma–krodha)
description: BhG 5.23, 5.26 (continuing 3.37–43): desire and anger as a pair whose surge (vega) must be withstood here before release from the body; the one who can is yoked and happy; freedom from both brings brahma-nirvāṇa near.

name: Passion, attachment (rāga)
description: BhG 4.10: freedom from passion (vīta-rāga), with freedom from fear and anger, marks those who came to the Lord's being.

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: BhG 4.10, 5.28, 6.14: those who came to the Lord's being were free of fear; the liberated sage is free of fear; the meditator sits free of fear (vigatabhīḥ).

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: BhG 5.3: the constant renunciant is the one who neither hates (dveṣṭi) nor desires.

name: Doubt (saṃśaya)
description: BhG 4.40–42: the doubting self perishes and has neither this world nor the next nor happiness; doubt is born of ignorance and lodged in the heart; the seers who attain brahma-nirvāṇa have their doubts cut (5.25); Arjuna asks the Lord to cut his doubt about the fallen yogin (6.39).
antidotes: the teacher who can cut the doubt (6.39)

name: Lack of faith (aśraddhā)
description: BhG 4.40: the faithless (aśraddadhāna), with the ignorant and the doubter, perishes; by contrast the one with faith obtains knowledge (4.39).

name: Ignorance (ajñāna)
description: BhG 5.15–16: ignorance covers knowledge, and by it creatures are deluded; when it is destroyed by knowledge of the self, knowledge illumines the highest like the sun. 4.42: doubt is born of ignorance. 4.40: the ignorant perishes.

name: Delusion (moha)
description: BhG 4.35: the knowledge taught by the seers removes delusion for good; 5.15: creatures are deluded because knowledge is covered by ignorance; 5.20: the knower of Brahman is undeluded.

name: The pairs of opposites (dvandva)
description: BhG 4.22, 5.3, 6.7: the one beyond the pairs is not bound though acting; free of them one is easily released from bondage; the conquered self stays composed amid cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.

name: Attachment to the fruits of action (phala-saṅga)
description: BhG 4–6: the Lord has no longing for the fruit of action (4.14); abandoning attachment to the fruit, one does nothing though acting (4.20); the unyoked one, attached to the fruit, is bound (5.12); the renunciant and yogin acts without depending on the fruit (6.1).

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: BhG 4–6: for the one whose attachment is gone action dissolves (4.23); one acting with actions placed in Brahman and abandoning attachment is unstained (5.10); yogins act abandoning attachment (5.11); one unattached to external contacts finds happiness in the self (5.21); one unattached to sense objects and actions has ascended to yoga (6.4).

name: Restlessness of mind
description: BhG 6.26, 6.33–35: the mind is restless (cañcala) and unsteady and wanders; Arjuna says it is turbulent, strong and obstinate, as hard to restrain as the wind, so that he cannot see the steady standing of the yoga of sameness; the Lord grants that it is hard to restrain.
antidotes: bringing the mind back to the self each time it wanders (6.26)

name: Stain, impurity, fault (kalmaṣa, kilbiṣa, pāpa)
description: BhG 4–6: impurities are destroyed by sacrifice (4.30); the worst sinner crosses all wrong by the raft of knowledge (4.36); stains are shaken off by knowledge (5.17) and destroyed in the seers who attain brahma-nirvāṇa (5.25); the one acting with actions placed in Brahman is not stained by sin (5.10); one doing merely bodily action incurs no fault (4.21); the calm yogin is stainless (6.27–28); the striving yogin is cleansed of faults over many births (6.45).

name: Envy (matsara)
description: BhG 4.22: the one free of envy (vimatsara), content with what comes unsought and beyond the opposites, is not bound though acting.

name: Excess or deficiency in food and sleep (BhG 6.16)
description: BhG 6.16: yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all, nor for one given to too much sleep, nor for one who stays awake too long.

name: Enjoyments born of contact (saṃsparśaja bhoga)
description: BhG 5.21–22: enjoyments born of contact are wombs of suffering and have a beginning and an end; the wise do not delight in them; the one unattached to external contacts finds happiness in the self.
